Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, upon his family and his Companions, and upon those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly meeting called the "Open Door Meeting," the ninety-ninth. It is held on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year 1416 AH. In it we speak, as God Almighty wills, about the tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) of Surat al-'Asr.

God Almighty says: ﴿By the 'Asr (time). Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1–2]. What is meant by "al-'Asr"?

It has been said that what is meant by al-'Asr is the end of the day, because the end of the day is its most virtuous part, and the 'Asr prayer is called the "middle prayer" (al-salah al-wusta), meaning the most excellent prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said that al-'Asr is time itself, and this is the more correct view: that al-'Asr is time. God swore by it because of the changing conditions that occur in it, the turning of affairs, the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and spoken of regarding the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods differ: hardship and ease, war and peace, health and sickness, righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things known to everyone.

What did God swear by it upon? Upon His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. "Mankind" here is general, because what is meant is the whole species. The sign of an "insan" (human) that is meant in a general sense is that the word "kull" (every) can take the place of "al" (the definite article). So here, if it were said, "Every human being is in loss," that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that God swore an oath concerning the state of mankind, that they are in loss, that is, in loss and deficiency in all their circumstances, in this world and the Hereafter, except those whom God Almighty excepted. As you see, this sentence is emphasized with three emphatic devices: first, the oath; second, ﴿إِنَّ﴾ ("indeed"); and third, the lam. He said ﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ ("in loss") so that it would be more eloquent than saying "لَخاسِرٌ" ("surely a loser"). This is because "في" ("in") means what? It means containment, as if mankind were immersed in loss, with loss encompassing him from every side.

﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, advise one another to the truth, and advise one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. God, Glorious and Exalted, excepted those who possess these four attributes.

The first attribute: faith that is not touched by doubt or hesitation. Faith in what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith. He said: "That you believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in the divine decree (qadar), its good and its evil" [[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both.]]. Explaining this hadith would take long if we spoke about it now, but we have spoken about it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be faith with no doubt or hesitation, meaning that you believe in these things as though you see them with your own eyes.

People in this matter are of three kinds:

The first: a sincere believer, with faith containing no doubt or hesitation.

The second: a disbeliever who denies and rejects.

The third: one who hesitates.

Which of these three kinds is saved? The saved one is the first, who believes with faith that contains no hesitation. He believes in God: in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah), and other things known of the attributes of the Lord, Mighty and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world. God Almighty created them from light and assigned them tasks, some known and some not known. Jibril, peace be upon him, is entrusted with revelation, descending with it from God to the prophets and messengers. Mika'il is entrusted with rain and plants, meaning God appointed him over the rain and everything connected with rain, and over vegetation. Israfil is appointed to blow the Trumpet. Malik is appointed over the Fire, and Ridwan over Paradise. Among the angels are some whose names we do not know, and whose tasks we also do not know. But it came in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is not a space of four fingers in the heavens except that an angel is standing, bowing, or prostrating to God" [[Al-Tirmidhi (2312) narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven groans, and it has every right to groan; there is not a space of four fingers in it but an angel has placed his forehead in prostration to God. By God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, you would not take pleasure in women on your beds, and you would go out to the open roads, crying out to God." [Abu Dharr said:] "I wish I were a tree that is cut down." The phrase "I wish I were a tree that is cut down" is from the words of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]].

Likewise we believe in the books that God sent down upon the messengers, peace be upon them. We believe in the messengers: those whom God related to us, we believe in them by name, and those whom He did not relate to us, we believe in them in general, because God did not relate to us all the accounts of the messengers. God Almighty said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day when people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and buhm" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among us delivering an exhortation and said: "O people, you will be gathered to God barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We are to do so﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104]..." to the end of the hadith. As for the word "buhm," it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, may God be pleased with him, in which: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection—or he said: the servants—naked, uncircumcised, buhm."]]. "Barefoot" means those who have no sandals or shoes, that is, their feet are bare; "naked" means those who have no clothes; "ghurl" are those who were not circumcised; and "buhm" are those who have no wealth with them. They will be gathered like that. "When the Prophet, peace be upon him, related that they would be naked, 'A'ishah said: 'O Messenger of God, will men and women look at one another?' He said: 'The matter is graver than that'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains to 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of God, women and men together, looking at one another?" He (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'ishah, the matter is more severe than that they should look at one another." As for the word "buhm," it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, may God be pleased with him, in which: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection—or he said: the servants—naked, uncircumcised, buhm."]]; that is, graver than their looking at one another, because each person will be preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may God have mercy on him, said: Part of faith in the Last Day is faith in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) reported of what happens after death. So you must believe in the trial of the grave, that is, the test that comes to the dead person when he is buried and his companions turn away from him: two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his prophet [[Abu Dawud (4753) narrated with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before the niche was dug. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat and we sat around him as if birds were on our heads, and in his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge in God from the punishment of the grave," twice or three times. In the hadith of Jarir he added here: And he said: "He hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?..." to the end of the hadith.]]. You also believe that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire [[Al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) narrated with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]], meaning that in it is punishment or reward. You likewise believe in Paradise and the Fire. Everything connected with the Last Day is included in our saying: that you believe in God and the Last Day.

Al-Qadar (divine decree) is God Almighty's decreeing. That is, you must believe that God Almighty decreed everything. This is because "God created the Pen and said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'And what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection'" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "The first thing God created was the Pen. He said: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write the decree, what has been and what will be, forever.'"]]. So in that hour it flowed with what will be until the Day of Resurrection.

So faith in His saying ﴿except those who believe﴾ includes what? Faith in the six foundations which the Messenger, peace be upon him, explained.

As for His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds such as prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, kindness to parents, maintaining family ties, and so on. They did not limit themselves to what is merely in the heart; rather, they acted and produced results.

Righteous deeds are those that combine two things: first, sincerity to God; second, following the Messenger, peace be upon him. This is because a deed that is not sincerely for God is rejected. God, Blessed and Exalted, said in the hadith qudsi that the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners, needing no partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates someone else with Me, I abandon him and his partnership" [[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him.]]. So if you stood to pray to show off to people, or gave charity to show off to people, or sought knowledge to show off to people, or maintained family ties to show off to people, or anything else, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous, that is, in its outward form.

Likewise following: if you did a deed that the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not do, and sought nearness to God by it with sincerity to God, it would not be accepted from you, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) similarly, and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being Muslim's, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her.]].

So the righteous deed is that which combines two descriptions: first, sincerity to God; and second, what? Following the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿and advise one another to the truth﴾ means that they came to advise one another to the truth, and the truth is the Shari'ah (divine law). That is, each of them advises the other: if he sees him neglecting an obligation, he advises him, saying: "My brother, benefit yourself, perform the obligation." If he sees him doing something forbidden, he advises him, saying: "My brother, avoid the forbidden." So they did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves; rather, they benefited themselves and others. ﴿They advised one another to the truth﴾: "the truth" here means what? The Shari'ah, which they advise one another to follow.

﴿and advise one another to patience﴾. Patience (sabr) is restraining the self from what should not be done. The people of knowledge divided it into three kinds, saying: patience is patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from what God has forbidden, and patience with God's decrees. Three kinds.

Patience in obedience: many people have laziness about praying in congregation, for example. He does not go to the mosque, saying: "I pray at home and I have fulfilled the obligation." He is lazy. We say: "My brother, make yourself patient, restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation."

Many people, when they see that the zakah on their wealth is large, become stingy and miserly and start hesitating: "Shall I take out this large sum, or leave it, or take it out later?" and the like. We say: "My brother, make yourself patient, force yourself to pay the zakah."

And so it is with the rest of the acts of worship. For worship is, as God Almighty said about prayer: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You find that most of God's servants find acts of worship heavy upon them, so they advise one another to patience: "Be patient in obedience, do not tire, do not be lazy."

Likewise patience in refraining from disobedience. Some people's selves draw them to forbidden earnings, whether through usury (riba), or through cheating and lying, or through deception, or other kinds of the forbidden. So we say: "Be patient, my brother, make yourself patient, do not deal in a forbidden way."

Some people are also tested with looking at women. You find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: "My brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this."

Patience with God's decrees: a person is afflicted with illness in his body, a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth, a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he becomes impatient, resentful, and pained. So they advise one another: "Be patient, my brother, this is a decreed matter, and impatience benefits nothing, and continued grief does not remove grief. Be patient; suppose this thing had never been at all." For example, a person lost a million riyals and grieved over it and suffered. What do we say to him? We say: "Be patient, my brother, suppose this million never existed. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on? Suppose this never was."

Likewise children. For example, a person is tested with the death of his son. We say: "My brother, be patient, suppose this son was never created." Then, as the Messenger, peace be upon him, said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward from God, for to God belongs what He took and to Him belongs what He gave" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains from Usamah ibn Zayd, may God be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when one of his daughters sent for him, calling him and informing him that a boy of hers, or a son of hers, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Go back to her and tell her that to God belongs what He took and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So tell her to be patient and to seek reward from God..." to the end of the hadith.]]. The whole matter belongs to God; it is not yours. So if God Almighty takes what is His own, how can you blame your Lord? How can you be resentful?

These are the kinds of patience: the first, patience in obeying God; the second, patience in refraining from disobeying God; and the third, patience with God's decrees.

Which of them is hardest on the soul? This differs. For some people, performing obedience is hard and very heavy on them. For some it is the opposite: obedience is easy for them, but abandoning disobedience is difficult and very hard on them. And for some people, patience in obedience and patience in refraining from disobedience are easy, but they cannot bear patience with calamities and are unable, to the point that their state may reach apostasy, and we seek refuge in God, as God Almighty said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships God on an edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

So, from this verse we learn that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, affirmed by an oath, reinforced with "inna" (indeed) and the lām, that all the children of Adam are what? Losers. Indeed, they are in loss; loss surrounds them from every side, except for those who are characterized by these four attributes: faith, righteous deeds, mutual counsel to the truth, and mutual counsel to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "If Allah had not sent down to His servants any proof except this surah, it would have sufficed them." He means: it would have sufficed them as an admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation; there is no purification in it, no prayer, no zakah, no Hajj and no fasting. But it would have sufficed them as an admonition. Every rational person knows that he is in loss unless he is characterized by these four attributes, and so he will strive, as far as he is able, to be characterized by these four attributes.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the successful who are granted divine guidance.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, upon his family and his Companions, and upon those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

If he sees him doing something forbidden, he advises him, saying: "My brother, avoid the forbidden." So they did not limit themselves to benefiting themselves; rather, they benefited themselves and others. ﴿They advised one another to the truth﴾: "the truth" here means what? The Shari'ah, which they advise one another to follow.

﴿and advise one another to patience﴾. Patience (sabr) is restraining the self from what should not be done. The people of knowledge divided it into three kinds, saying: patience is patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from what God has forbidden, and patience with God's decrees. Three kinds.

Patience in obedience: many people have laziness about praying in congregation, for example. He does not go to the mosque, saying: "I pray at home and I have fulfilled the obligation." He is lazy. We say: "My brother, make yourself patient, restrain it, compel it to pray in congregation."

Many people, when they see that the zakah on their wealth is large, become stingy and miserly and start hesitating: "Shall I take out this large sum, or leave it, or take it out later?" and the like. We say: "My brother, make yourself patient, force yourself to pay the zakah."

And so it is with the rest of the acts of worship. For worship is, as God Almighty said about prayer: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humble﴾ [al-Baqarah 45]. You find that most of God's servants find acts of worship heavy upon them, so they advise one another to patience: "Be patient in obedience, do not tire, do not be lazy."

Likewise patience in refraining from disobedience. Some people's selves draw them to forbidden earnings, whether through usury (riba), or through cheating and lying, or through deception, or other kinds of the forbidden. So we say: "Be patient, my brother, make yourself patient, do not deal in a forbidden way."

Some people are also tested with looking at women. You find him walking in the market, and whenever a woman passes he follows her with his gaze. We say: "My brother, be patient, restrain yourself from this."

Patience with God's decrees: a person is afflicted with illness in his body, a person is afflicted with the loss of some of his wealth, a person is afflicted with the loss of his loved ones, and he becomes impatient, resentful, and pained. So they advise one another: "Be patient, my brother, this is a decreed matter, and impatience benefits nothing, and continued grief does not remove grief. Be patient; suppose this thing had never been at all." For example, a person lost a million riyals and grieved over it and suffered. What do we say to him? We say: "Be patient, my brother, suppose this million never existed. Did you not come out of your mother's womb with no clothes on? Suppose this never was."

Likewise children. For example, a person is tested with the death of his son. We say: "My brother, be patient, suppose this son was never created." Then, as the Messenger, peace be upon him, said to one of his daughters: "Tell her to be patient and seek reward from God, for to God belongs what He took and to Him belongs what He gave" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (7448) and Muslim (923/11), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains from Usamah ibn Zayd, may God be pleased with them both, who said: We were with the Prophet (ﷺ) when one of his daughters sent for him, calling him and informing him that a boy of hers, or a son of hers, was dying. He said to the messenger: "Go back to her and tell her that to God belongs what He took and to Him belongs what He gave, and everything with Him has an appointed term. So tell her to be patient and to seek reward from God..." to the end of the hadith.]]. The whole matter belongs to God; it is not yours. So if God Almighty takes what is His own, how can you blame your Lord? How can you be resentful?

These are the kinds of patience: the first, patience in obeying God; the second, patience in refraining from disobeying God; and the third, patience with God's decrees.

Which of them is hardest on the soul? This differs. For some people, performing obedience is hard and very heavy on them. For some it is the opposite: obedience is easy for them, but abandoning disobedience is difficult and very hard on them. And for some people, patience in obedience and patience in refraining from disobedience are easy, but they cannot bear patience with calamities and are unable, to the point that their state may reach apostasy, and we seek refuge in God, as God Almighty said: ﴿And among the people is he who worships God on an edge: if good befalls him, he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face. He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the clear loss﴾ [al-Hajj 11].

So, from this verse we learn that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, affirmed by an oath, reinforced with "inna" (indeed) and the lām, that all the children of Adam are what? Losers. Indeed, they are in loss; loss surrounds them from every side, except for those who are characterized by these four attributes: faith, righteous deeds, mutual counsel to the truth, and mutual counsel to patience.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "If Allah had not sent down to His servants any proof except this surah, it would have sufficed them." He means: it would have sufficed them as an admonition, not as legislation, because there is nothing in it of legislation; there is no purification in it, no prayer, no zakah, no Hajj and no fasting. But it would have sufficed them as an admonition. Every rational person knows that he is in loss unless he is characterized by these four attributes, and so he will strive, as far as he is able, to be characterized by these four attributes.

We ask Allah to make us and you among the successful who are granted divine guidance.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and may God send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, upon his family and his Companions, and upon those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the weekly meeting called the "Open Door Meeting," the ninety-ninth. It is held on Thursday, the fourteenth of Rabi' al-Awwal, in the year 1416 AH. In it we speak, as God Almighty wills, about the tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) of Surat al-'Asr.

God Almighty says: ﴿By the 'Asr (time). Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ [al-'Asr 1–2]. What is meant by "al-'Asr"?

It has been said that what is meant by al-'Asr is the end of the day, because the end of the day is its most virtuous part, and the 'Asr prayer is called the "middle prayer" (al-salah al-wusta), meaning the most excellent prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ) named it.

And it has been said that al-'Asr is time itself, and this is the more correct view: that al-'Asr is time. God swore by it because of the changing conditions that occur in it, the turning of affairs, the alternation of days among people, and other things that are witnessed in the present and spoken of regarding the past. So al-'Asr is the time in which creation lives, and its periods differ: hardship and ease, war and peace, health and sickness, righteous deeds and evil deeds, and other things known to everyone.

What did God swear by it upon? Upon His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. "Mankind" here is general, because what is meant is the whole species. The sign of an "insan" (human) that is meant in a general sense is that the word "kull" (every) can take the place of "al" (the definite article). So here, if it were said, "Every human being is in loss," that would be the meaning.

The meaning of the noble verse is that God swore an oath concerning the state of mankind, that they are in loss, that is, in loss and deficiency in all their circumstances, in this world and the Hereafter, except those whom God Almighty excepted. As you see, this sentence is emphasized with three emphatic devices: first, the oath; second, ﴿إِنَّ﴾ ("indeed"); and third, the lam. He said ﴿لَفِي خُسْرٍ﴾ ("in loss") so that it would be more eloquent than saying "لَخاسِرٌ" ("surely a loser"). This is because "في" ("in") means what? It means containment, as if mankind were immersed in loss, with loss encompassing him from every side.

﴿Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, advise one another to the truth, and advise one another to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 3]. God, Glorious and Exalted, excepted those who possess these four attributes.

The first attribute: faith that is not touched by doubt or hesitation. Faith in what? In what the Messenger (ﷺ) explained when Jibril asked him about faith. He said: "That you believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in the divine decree (qadar), its good and its evil" [[Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may God be pleased with them both.]]. Explaining this hadith would take long if we spoke about it now, but we have spoken about it in many places. Those who believe in these six foundations are the believers, but it must be faith with no doubt or hesitation, meaning that you believe in these things as though you see them with your own eyes.

People in this matter are of three kinds:

The first: a sincere believer, with faith containing no doubt or hesitation.

The second: a disbeliever who denies and rejects.

The third: one who hesitates.

Which of these three kinds is saved? The saved one is the first, who believes with faith that contains no hesitation. He believes in God: in His existence, His names, His attributes, His divinity (uluhiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah), and other things known of the attributes of the Lord, Mighty and Exalted. He believes in the angels, who are an unseen world. God Almighty created them from light and assigned them tasks, some known and some not known. Jibril, peace be upon him, is entrusted with revelation, descending with it from God to the prophets and messengers. Mika'il is entrusted with rain and plants, meaning God appointed him over the rain and everything connected with rain, and over vegetation. Israfil is appointed to blow the Trumpet. Malik is appointed over the Fire, and Ridwan over Paradise. Among the angels are some whose names we do not know, and whose tasks we also do not know. But it came in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "there is not a space of four fingers in the heavens except that an angel is standing, bowing, or prostrating to God" [[Al-Tirmidhi (2312) narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven groans, and it has every right to groan; there is not a space of four fingers in it but an angel has placed his forehead in prostration to God. By God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much, you would not take pleasure in women on your beds, and you would go out to the open roads, crying out to God." [Abu Dharr said:] "I wish I were a tree that is cut down." The phrase "I wish I were a tree that is cut down" is from the words of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him; see Musnad Ahmad (21516).]].

Likewise we believe in the books that God sent down upon the messengers, peace be upon them. We believe in the messengers: those whom God related to us, we believe in them by name, and those whom He did not relate to us, we believe in them in general, because God did not relate to us all the accounts of the messengers. God Almighty said: ﴿Among them are those We have related to you, and among them are those We have not related to you﴾ [Ghafir 78].

The Last Day is the Day of Resurrection, the day when people come out of their graves for recompense, "barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and buhm" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3349) and Muslim (2860/58), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood among us delivering an exhortation and said: "O people, you will be gathered to God barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us. Indeed, We are to do so﴾ [al-Anbiya' 104]..." to the end of the hadith. As for the word "buhm," it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, may God be pleased with him, in which: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection—or he said: the servants—naked, uncircumcised, buhm."]]. "Barefoot" means those who have no sandals or shoes, that is, their feet are bare; "naked" means those who have no clothes; "ghurl" are those who were not circumcised; and "buhm" are those who have no wealth with them. They will be gathered like that. "When the Prophet, peace be upon him, related that they would be naked, 'A'ishah said: 'O Messenger of God, will men and women look at one another?' He said: 'The matter is graver than that'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56), the wording being Muslim's, with their chains to 'A'ishah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised." I said: "O Messenger of God, women and men together, looking at one another?" He (ﷺ) said: "O 'A'ishah, the matter is more severe than that they should look at one another." As for the word "buhm," it came in what Ahmad (16042) narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Unays, may God be pleased with him, in which: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection—or he said: the servants—naked, uncircumcised, buhm."]]; that is, graver than their looking at one another, because each person will be preoccupied with himself.

Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may God have mercy on him, said: Part of faith in the Last Day is faith in everything the Prophet (ﷺ) reported of what happens after death. So you must believe in the trial of the grave, that is, the test that comes to the dead person when he is buried and his companions turn away from him: two angels come to him and ask him about his Lord, his religion, and his prophet [[Abu Dawud (4753) narrated with his chain from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) at the funeral of a man from the Ansar, and we reached the grave before the niche was dug. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat and we sat around him as if birds were on our heads, and in his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge in God from the punishment of the grave," twice or three times. In the hadith of Jarir he added here: And he said: "He hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away, when it is said to him: O so-and-so, who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?..." to the end of the hadith.]]. You also believe that the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire [[Al-Tabarani in al-Awsat (8613) narrated with his chain from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire."]], meaning that in it is punishment or reward. You likewise believe in Paradise and the Fire. Everything connected with the Last Day is included in our saying: that you believe in God and the Last Day.

Al-Qadar (divine decree) is God Almighty's decreeing. That is, you must believe that God Almighty decreed everything. This is because "God created the Pen and said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'And what shall I write?' He said: 'Write what will be until the Day of Resurrection'" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2155) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, with the wording: "The first thing God created was the Pen. He said: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'Write the decree, what has been and what will be, forever.'"]]. So in that hour it flowed with what will be until the Day of Resurrection.

So faith in His saying ﴿except those who believe﴾ includes what? Faith in the six foundations which the Messenger, peace be upon him, explained.

As for His saying ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, its meaning is that they performed righteous deeds such as prayer, zakah, fasting, Hajj, kindness to parents, maintaining family ties, and so on. They did not limit themselves to what is merely in the heart; rather, they acted and produced results.

Righteous deeds are those that combine two things: first, sincerity to God; second, following the Messenger, peace be upon him. This is because a deed that is not sincerely for God is rejected. God, Blessed and Exalted, said in the hadith qudsi that the Prophet (ﷺ) narrates from Him: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners, needing no partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates someone else with Me, I abandon him and his partnership" [[Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him.]]. So if you stood to pray to show off to people, or gave charity to show off to people, or sought knowledge to show off to people, or maintained family ties to show off to people, or anything else, the deed is rejected even if it is righteous, that is, in its outward form.

Likewise following: if you did a deed that the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not do, and sought nearness to God by it with sincerity to God, it would not be accepted from you, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) similarly, and Muslim (1718/18), the wording being Muslim's, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her.]].

So the righteous deed is that which combines two descriptions: first, sincerity to God; and second, what? Following the Messenger (ﷺ).
